changes.before: Role and work-area choices suggest useful connections to your work. They do not restrict participation. Clear your choices to explore the full library. Learning levels describe courses; choose all levels to include practical tools and references.
changes.after: Role and work-area selections help highlight relevant resources, but do not limit which materials you may use. Clearing your choices allows you to see the full collection of resources. Learning levels are used for courses; selecting all levels will include additional tools and references that do not have a course structure.
changes.reason: Clarifies how role and work-area choices affect resource visibility and explains why clearing choices is useful. Explains that learning levels apply to courses specifically, and why a staff member would select all levels.

findings.finding: The proposed text (field8) changes the meaning and slightly broadens the scope, drifting from the established source wording. Source: "Role and work-area choices suggest useful connections to your work. They do not restrict participation. Clear your choices to explore the full library. Learning levels describe courses; choose all levels to include practical tools and references." Proposed: "Role and work-area selections help highlight relevant resources, but do not limit which materials you may use. Clearing your choices allows you to see the full collection of resources. Learning levels are used for courses; selecting all levels will include additional tools and references that do not have a course structure." Issues: (1) The change from "do not restrict participation" to "do not limit which materials you may use" is less precise and may imply a technical limitation that does not exist in the source. (2) The reworded lines over-explain audience options and add interpretive detail about "tools and references that do not have a course structure" that goes beyond the source phrase "practical tools and references." (3) The language shifts from instructional/contextual to descriptive/interpretive, which is not permitted for protected content. (4) "Clearing your choices allows you to see..." replaces "Clear your choices to explore..." shifting proactive instruction to a description, which could lose a practical nuance. (5) The proposal omits the phrase "Learning levels describe courses," instead splitting the explanation in a way that slightly changes the instructional character.
